Ravi (PM): Quick sync on API Keys UX — focusing on create/generate, rotate, revoke, and empty-state copy. Need final copy + a11y checks by end of week. Figma: https://figma.redwood/keys-v2 :sparkles:

June (Design): Main visual problems: 1) the create modal currently has two visually heavy CTAs which competes for attention. 2) when we reveal the secret we swap the modal for a small ephemeral drawer but the tab/focus order flips awkwardly. 3) empty-state reads too product-y  needs simpler helper and clearer CTA.

Priya (UX Writer): Proposed CTA hierarchy: primary = 'Generate key', secondary = 'Reveal secret' (low-contrast). After generation show a short ephemeral panel titled 'Secret — copy now' with two actions: 'Copy secret' and 'Close'. Short banner suggestion (compact): "Secret visible only once. Save it now." Longer variant for docs: "This secret is shown only at creation. Store it somewhere safe  we cant retrieve it later"

Noah (Frontend): Reminder: server only returns the token on create. We must make that explicit. Implementation notes: set focus to the secret <input> on drawer open, enable keyboard copy shortcut, ensure aria-live region announces the one-time warning. Also avoid auto-closing the drawer immediately after copy; give users a clear Close button.

Maya (Accessibility): A11y checklist: 1) focus trap flow: modal -> drawer focus landing on secret input/button. 2) use aria-live="polite" for the one-time notice so screen readers get it without interrupting. 3) color contrast: current warning amber icon fails AA on light bg; bump to token amber-600 or add outline. 4) disabled rotate control needs an accessible explanation (aria-describedby) and keyboard focusable tooltip trigger.

June (Design): Empty state copy idea: headline: "No API keys yet"; subcopy: "API keys let apps call Redwood. Create scoped keys for least privilege." Primary CTA: "Create your first key" (opens modal). Use a minimal illustration and avoid auto-launching modals on first visit.

Ravi (PM): Permissions and rotate UX: show Rotate button even if user lacks perms, but render disabled. The disabled control should expose a clear reason via tooltip and aria attributes.

Priya (UX Writer): Tooltip copy (short): "Requires Key Admin role. Request access from an org admin." Keep <80 chars. aria-label for disabled button: "Rotate key (requires Key Admin role)". Give a second microcopy variant: "Rotate (admin role required)" for narrow buttons.

Noah (Frontend): Revoke / delete flow: engineering prefers a checkbox "I acknowledge this revokes access" + optional freeform Reason field. Avoid forcing users to type the exact key name for destructive ops (hurts keyboard/sr users). Log the reason to audit service if provided.

Maya (Accessibility): Agreed on checkbox + optional reason. Ensure checkbox has programmatic label and error messages are announced. If we surface validation (e.g., empty reason allowed) keep announcements consistent.

ui-bot: Design checklist entry created: https://figma.redwood/keys-checklist-v2 (focus order, toast timing, contrast tokens). :white_check_mark:

Ravi (PM): Next steps: @June drop final screens with focus states, @Priya deliver short+long variants and the tooltip strings, @Maya will run quick a11y pass once PR is up, @Noah coordinate the focus/clipboard behavior. Thanks all! :rocket:
